rubric_notes: Verified 2.08 lineage, homology endpoint, annotations, five families with sunids, TAF and core-histone children, single superfamily under a.22. Correctly frames the relationship as superfamily-level homology (probable common ancestry) and not family-level, notes fold/class alone indicate structure not ancestry, and refuses to transfer function, DNA-binding mode, nucleosome assembly or templates. Correctly says SCOPe makes no homology assertion for H1/H5 or histone-modifying enzymes rather than asserting non-homology. Scopes unexamined items (SIDs, hits, quality). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

All classifications and identifiers match the bundle. Lowest shared level correctly identified as superfamily, interpreted as probable common ancestry more distant than family; rejects both directions of function transfer, template use, and over-reading of Li/UNL ligands; notes 7-93 partial-chain boundary and no warnings/heterogeneity. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

All three families and sunids, superfamily 53067, fold 53066, class 51349 supported by bundle; homology endpoint (homology_implied_by_level true, scope sf, no warnings) and the duplication comment are both in the bundle and correctly interpreted. Remote homology inference, duplicated RNase H-like core forming ATP cleft, and explicit rejection of substrate, reaction, regulation, oligomeric state, active-site residues, mechanism and template transfer. Fold-level grouping correctly described as structural only. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct, bundle-supported hierarchy and SUNIDs; heme catalase placement in e.5.1.1 supported by the catalase search. Good divergent-evolution interpretation, explicit refusal to assign ferroxidase/catalase activity to half-ferritin or unknown members, and template caveats. Does not state what evidence (sequence, structural, experimental) would be needed to assign metal ligands, chemistry, or role, only that superfamily membership alone is insufficient. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

All identifiers (49504, 74874, 110105, 110107, 110108, 49503, 49502, 48724, d5n0ya1), the b.6.1 children, superfamily homology scope 'sf', and the 'contains copper-binding site' / 'mono-domain proteins' comments are in the bundle and interpreted correctly. Rejects copper/electron-transfer inference, requires ligand/metal/biochemical evidence, and explicitly avoids both the analogy claim and fold-as-function error. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct d.15.1.1/d.15.1.2/d.15.1.5 under d.15.1 (sunids 54237/54250/54263/54236), fold d.15, class d, all supported by bundle; homology_implied_by_level at sf and empty annotations correctly reported. States probable common ancestry and shared beta-grasp scaffold, distinguishes family vs superfamily closeness, explicitly rejects conjugation, UBX->Ras and RBD->p97 transfers, fold-alone-not-ancestry, and states limits of retrieved data. No material issues.

All three families, superfamily, fold and sunids correct and supported; example domains d1u0sy_ (T. maritima CheY), d1c4ka1/d1orda1 (1-107), d1m2ea_, d1r8ja2 (2-135) verified in bundle; correctly identifies ODC catalytic domains as c.67.1.5 and d.125.1.1 in different folds; homology no-warning and 'CASP5' comment supported, and it is transparent about not retrieving an ODC /parents record. Reasoning covers remote ancestry at superfamily level, domain recruitment into different multidomain proteins, and explicitly rejects transfer of phosphorylation/two-component signaling, catalysis, KaiC regulation, CheY chemotaxis role, templates, and the idea that CheY signaling is ancestral. No material issues. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Complete: b.84.5 (310577), b.84.5.1 (310616), protein nodes, example domains with boundaries (d3a5ca3, d1vdza2, d3j9ta3) all verified in bundle. Explains that fold level records architecture only (quotes fold-level warning), superfamily asserts common ancestry among V1/A1 bulge domains only, and that separate superfamilies do not imply analogy or convergence. Appropriately flags that the curators' rationale is inference. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Fold f.21 (81344), fold comment, three superfamilies with sunids, and the fold-level homology record (homology_implied_by_level false, warning) are all supported by the bundle. Explicitly states separate superfamilies are not proof of analogy/convergence, rejects function/heme-number/template transfer, and lists what was not retrieved. Minor imprecision: calls cytochrome b6 and mitochondrial cytochrome b 'families' (they are proteins in f.21.1.2); f.21.3.1/103502 and d1q16c_/d1y4zc_ are not in the bundle but are correct. Evidence types needed are stated somewhat generically (sequence, structure, literature). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct identifiers for all three families, superfamily, fold and class, all supported by bundle. Superfamily = probable common ancestry of Rossmann core; family separation = remote relationship and functional divergence; explicitly says substrate, reaction, cofactor and physiological role must be established independently per family, and that a channel Rossmann domain need not be an oxidoreductase. Correctly rejects both 'analogous/convergent' and 'same function' readings. Transparent about background-knowledge descriptions. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Lineage and identifiers correct and the designed-protein caveat is given. But it affirmatively claims there is 'no nf (not-a-true-fold) or similar flag' and that 'no returned caveat undermines the same-family placement' after checking only domain-level endpoints; the family node 100905 carries 'not a true family', which directly contradicts that assurance. Answers 'Yes, classified as homologous' relying on the generic level semantics the annotation overrides. Bio ceiling 2; factual 2.

Verified 1.69 (d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 own fold, sunids) and 2.08 (d1t1ja1 c.23.14.2 vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1 under shared 52309) with correct interpretation: different folds to probable common ancestry at superfamily level, family-level relationship withheld, no function/template transfer. Minor imprecision: describes the 'a1' SID suffix as 'discontinuous-style', which is not what the suffix denotes; noncentral.

Identifies d1a14h2 as H:1-8 synthetic N-terminal tag, class l, l.1.1.1 with full lineage and sunids all supported by bundle. d1a14h1 H:9-111 correctly given as b.1.1.1 VH with lineage and Fab NC10 comment supported. Cites homology_implied_by_level=false and artifact_not_homology_evidence warning. Clearly rejects tag similarity as ancestry evidence, directs homology inference to d1a14h1, and states limits (sequence not verified). No must_avoid violations.

Full 1.75 and 2.08 facts correct with excellent caveats: calcium binding is not evidence of shared origin, BLAST/FATCAT hits are comparison not assignment, and absence of a hit is not absence of relationship. Honestly omits the 2.04 split pinpoint.

Complete and fully evidence-supported: five domains with correct boundaries and lineages, bromodomain correctly flagged as family-level homology, three Prp8-specific families in known superfamilies, d3jb9a5 d.394 as new fold. Mosaic interpretation plus explicit limits on function transfer, nonhomology between domains, and acquisition order. Minor phrasing slip ('three of the five SIDs numbered in reverse') is immaterial. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Full lineage with sunids, 're' annotation, 'single repeat', canonical repeat representative with coordinate caveat, absence of 're' on d4cj9a_, no homology warnings. Correct interpretation that length reflects repeat count, with explicit limits and honest note that lengths were not retrieved.

Correct metadata and periodic label (bundle-supported). Cites stable 2.08, pins release in calls instead of the moving 'current' alias, records periodic string if used. States periodic is stable version plus update date, does not replace or create a stable release. Omits that periodic updates add newly classified PDB entries without rewriting stable domains. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Complete and evidence-backed: correct a.47.2.1 placement for all domains, lineage sunids, automated-matches node and comment for d1dn1b_, fragment comment and 'ms' flag for d1br0a_/d1ez3a_, no homology warnings, plus a supported 2.01 lineage check. Interpretation correctly frames the fragment assignment as a statement about the partial structure, notes a three-helix piece generically resembles a spectrin repeat, grounds family placement in protein identity and the full-domain structure, and keeps fold-level similarity distinct from homology. Declines function/template transfer and quality ranking without data. Does not mention the fourth helix explicitly, but the missing-secondary-structure point covers it.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. All cited facts (c.2/51734, c.2.1/51735, c.3.1/51905, c.4.1/51971, NamA c.1.4.1/141763) match the bundle. Correctly distinguishes divergence within c.2.1 from possible convergence or undetectable remote relationship across folds, states SCOPe placement cannot decide between them, and lists the independent evidence needed. Covers motif/active-site convergence, modularity of domains, and transfer limits. No must_avoid violations.

Accurate classifications and SUNIDs for both releases; 2.04 shared only class, 2.08 same fold/superfamily b.18.1 with separate families b.18.1.36 vs b.18.1.3. Structure-led remote-homology framing, notes rationale not in API, rejects function and template transfer. Chain B split and l.1.1.1 noted correctly.

Lineage with sunids, boundaries, comments, and hf definition all supported by the bundle. Correctly separates family/homology label from fold/structure label, keeps homology intact, rejects interchangeable template and training use, recommends flagging/stratifying with caveat preserved, and notes mutant/ligand state and that the specific fold difference is unverified. Quality scores correctly described as not addressing the evolutionary question. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 judge, 2026-10-22.

Meets all must_include: homology retained at family level; fr flag correctly defined (missing >1/3 common structure) and tied to partial alignment coverage and non-comparable scores; complete unflagged domain (d1uc6a1) preferred as representative conditional on quality, fragment retained with label for protein/species coverage. Lineage, sunids, boundaries, comment and homology-endpoint facts all supported by bundle. Explicitly declines quality ranking without retrieved quality records and rejects function transfer. Clear limits stated. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Correct recommendation; new family in existing superfamily is a positive homology claim needing core-position sequence, motif/active-site or alignment evidence; new superfamily is a limited 'no SCOPe homology assertion', not analogy/convergence, revisable; new fold would overstate novelty given fold resemblance and requires differing arrangement/topology; fold match, FATCAT hit, shared ligand or name not homology evidence; no function/template transfer. No fabricated identifiers. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct 2.08 hierarchy with sunids (56112, 56111, 88854, 64411, 56171); homology_implied_by_level=true, no warnings, the ATP-grasp/PIPK comment and the d.15.15 ABD placement are all supported by the bundle. Distinguishes fold similarity from the superfamily ancestry claim, rejects substrate and regulation transfer and over-reading of cross-superfamily non-homology, and lists target alignment of catalytic/specificity motifs, biochemistry, ligand-bound structures, domain architecture, paralog context and the non-official status of BLAST/FATCAT hits. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.
